muye: The Battle of Muye, about 1046 BCE: the Zhou army with bronze dagger-axes, bronze-tipped spears and two-horse war chariots advances across a wide plain at dawn against a vast Shang host; banners of plain silk, leather armour, no stirrups. Rendered as an ink-and-colour painting on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, muted ochre, cinnabar and black, distant figures, no blood.
qin-unifies: 221 BCE, the Qin capital Xianyang: the newly proclaimed First Emperor's court in a vast rammed-earth palace with timber columns and black lacquer; officials in dark robes present bamboo slips, standard bronze weights, measures and round square-holed Ban Liang coins. Painted in the style of Han-dynasty tomb murals, flat colours of black, red and ochre on plaster, figures small and seen from a distance, no faces in close-up.
xuanzang: 629 CE: a Buddhist monk with a bamboo-framed pack of scrolls on his back walks a desert caravan trail past sand dunes and distant snow mountains, a horse and a few travellers far behind, a Silk Road oasis and stupa on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, flaking pigment texture.
wang-anshi: Kaifeng, capital of the Northern Song, about 1069: a bustling street by the Bian River with an arched timber bridge, cargo boats, tea houses, shop banners without legible writing, porters, ox carts and officials in robes; a government office gate where farmers queue for state grain loans. Painted as a long horizontal Northern Song handscroll in fine ink line and light colour on silk, in the manner of Along the River During the Qingming Festival, many tiny figures.
zheng-he: 1405: the Ming treasure fleet sets sail from the Yangtze estuary, great multi-masted junks with red-brown battened sails, smaller escort ships, flags flying, crowds on the riverbank. Painted as a Ming-dynasty ink and colour hanging scroll on silk, blue-green landscape style, waves drawn in fine repeating lines.
humen: 1839, Humen on the Pearl River estuary: Qing officials in court robes and hats with officers and labourers supervise trenches on the shore where chests of opium are broken open and dissolved with lime and salt and flushed into the sea; forts on the hills, foreign sailing ships far off. Painted as a nineteenth-century Canton export painting, gouache on paper, clear daylight, many small figures.
yu-founds-xia: c. 2070 BCE, Yangcheng in the Song mountain foothills: a broad river valley after a great flood, receding water channelled into newly dug ditches and earthen dykes; groups of workers in simple undyed hemp tunics carry baskets of earth and wooden spades; on a rise beside a cluster of thatched rammed-earth houses, an elder leader in plain robes stands small among kinsmen, a younger man at his side. Misty hills, morning light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, muted earth tones.
erlitou: c. 1900 BCE, Erlitou on the Yiluo river plain: a large rectangular rammed-earth palace platform with a timber-and-thatch hall, a walled courtyard and gateway, straight packed-earth roads with cart ruts beside it; nearby a bronze workshop where craftsmen pour molten bronze from clay crucibles into piece moulds, a small finished jue wine vessel and turquoise inlay pieces on a mat. Workers in plain hemp clothing, smoke rising, late afternoon. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette of black, cinnabar and ochre.
mingtiao: c. 1600 BCE, Mingtiao: two bronze-age armies meet on an open loess plain under a stormy sky; ranks of foot soldiers with bronze dagger-axes on long shafts and leather-and-wood shields, no chariots or horses, banners of plain coloured cloth; one army advances confidently while the other breaks and flees toward distant hills, seen from far away with small figures and rising dust, no wounds shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, ochre and cinnabar accents.
yin: c. 1300 BCE, the Huan River plain near Anyang: a long column of Shang people migrating to a new capital, carrying bronze ritual vessels on poles, ox carts loaded with baskets and jars, nobles in dark robes with wide sashes; ahead, workers ram earth between wooden boards to raise palace foundations of a new timber-and-thatch hall complex beside the river. Wide flat landscape, soft autumn light. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black ground with cinnabar and ochre figures.
oracle-bones: c. 1250 BCE, a Shang ritual hall at Yin: inside a dim timber hall with a thatched roof and rammed-earth floor, diviners in dark robes kneel around a small fire, holding a heated bronze rod to a prepared turtle plastron so it cracks; ox shoulder blades and turtle shells with carved notches lie on reed mats, a bronze ding cauldron and incense smoke nearby; a king figure seen from behind watches. Scratched marks too small to read. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of Chu silk paintings, warm firelight.
sanxingdui: c. 1200 BCE, Sanxingdui on the Chengdu plain: an open-air ceremony in a green, misty river landscape; a towering standing bronze figure with oversized hands, large bronze masks with protruding cylindrical eyes and huge ears set on wooden posts, a tall bronze sacred tree with birds; people in simple woven garments bring offerings of elephant tusks and jade blades, smoke from a fire pit. Bamboo groves and rice fields beyond. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and gold-ochre.
chengzhou: c. 1038 BCE, Luoyi on the Luo River: on a bluff above the river, a Western Zhou regent in dark ceremonial robe and tall cap, small and seen from behind among officials, surveys surveyors with plumb lines and workers ramming earth walls for a new city; groups of resettled Shang nobles in robes arrive with ox carts and bronze vessels; chariots wait nearby. Wide river valley, hills of the Mang range, clear morning. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
gonghe: 841 BCE, Haojing near the Feng River: a Western Zhou palace courtyard of timber halls on rammed-earth platforms with tiled ridges; a group of senior ministers in long robes and caps hold court around a bronze ding and bamboo-slip bundles, while an empty throne platform stands behind them; outside the gate, townspeople in hemp clothing gather quietly. Grey spring light, willows by the moat. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, faded mineral pigments.
haojing-falls: 771 BCE, Haojing in the Wei River valley at dusk: beacon fires burn on distant hilltop towers while dark smoke rises over the timber halls and earthen walls of the Zhou capital; seen from a far hillside, columns of horsemen and foot raiders in fur and leather from the western steppe pour across the plain, and refugees with carts flee east along the road. No close fighting shown. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre, dramatic red sky.
move-east: 770 BCE, the road to Luoyi: a long procession of the Zhou court travelling east through loess hills, horse-drawn chariots with parasols, ox carts heavy with bronze ritual vessels, bamboo-slip archives and chests, nobles in dark robes, escorts with dagger-axes from allied lords; ahead the Luo River valley and the walls of a waiting eastern city. Autumn colours, long winding road. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, soft wash.
duke-huan: 679 BCE, a conference of lords near Linzi in Qi: on a raised earthen altar platform in an open field, rulers of several states in long robes and tall caps stand in a ring around a bronze vessel for a covenant oath, attendants with banners and a sacrificial ox; chariots lined up below, the walled city of Linzi and the sea-facing plain beyond. Figures small, no faces in detail. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre on a pale ground.
guo-yu: 655 BCE, near Shangyang by the Yellow River gorges: a Jin army column of horse-drawn chariots and foot soldiers with dagger-axes winds along a mountain road through the small state of Yu, whose lords watch from a gatehouse; far ahead across the river valley, the walls of Guo's town under a pale winter sky. Loess cliffs and the curving Yellow River. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
chengpu: 632 BCE, Chengpu on the North China plain: two great chariot armies on a flat plain, Jin chariots driving forward, some horses draped in tiger-pattern cloths to frighten the enemy, dust raised by dragged branches; the Chu lines in red-and-black lacquered armour fall back toward the south. Seen from a distance, small figures, banners and clouds of dust, no wounds. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre, like a painted Chu lacquer box lid.
confucius: 551 BCE, Qufu in the state of Lu: a modest rammed-earth house with thatched roof by a quiet village lane near Mount Ni, a mother resting inside with a newborn swaddled in hemp cloth, an old father and a few relatives in plain robes at the doorway; scholarly bamboo-slip bundles on a shelf, willows and green hills, gentle dawn light. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, soft and calm.
wu-xu: 512 BCE, the state of Xu in the Huai River lowlands: seen from a distant hill, Wu soldiers in leather armour have built earthen dams and cut channels so river water floods around a walled town, its gate half submerged; boats with oarsmen circle, townspeople wade out carrying bundles. Reed marshes, rain clouds, grey water. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, cool watery tones.
boju: 506 BCE, Boju in the Han River country: a Wu army of foot soldiers with bronze swords and dagger-axes and a few chariots sweeps through wooded hills along a river, banners in hand; far off the Chu army retreats in disorder toward its capital Ying, smoke rising on the horizon. A general on a hill directs the march, small and seen from behind. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre.
yue-wu: 473 BCE, Gusu near Lake Tai: Yue soldiers in lacquered leather armour with bronze swords and boats crowd the canals and lake shore around the walled Wu capital, its towers and high terraces against an evening sky with thin smoke; a hut of brushwood in the foreground with a hanging gall, a quiet symbol of long endurance. Water country with reeds and willow. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, misty greens and greys.
jinyang: 453 BCE, Jinyang on the Fen River: the walled city stands in floodwater after besiegers diverted the river, roofs and walls rising from the water; on the surrounding earthen dykes the camps of besieging armies, and at night small boats slip out; in the distance the camp of one army is being swamped as dykes are cut. Seen from far above, small figures, moonlight on water. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
three-jin: 403 BCE, Jinyang: in a hall of timber pillars and rammed-earth walls, an envoy of the Zhou king in dark robes presents ritual bronzes and jade tokens to three lords in tall caps standing side by side, each with retainers; outside, three sets of banners and chariots wait in a courtyard. Figures modest in size, formal and calm, lamplight. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre.
han-zheng: 375 BCE, Xinzheng on the plain of central Henan: the Han army in iron and leather armour with crossbows and dagger-axes enters the gates of the walled city of Zheng, while court officials in robes lead a train of carts bringing archives and bronze vessels to set up a new capital; rammed-earth walls, watchtowers, flat farmland beyond. Seen from a distance, daylight. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
daliang: 361 BCE, Daliang on the eastern plain: a long column of the Wei court moving east with ox carts and chariots, officials in robes and caps, carrying bronze vessels and bamboo-slip archives; ahead, workers build the rammed-earth walls of a new capital beside a river and canals across a flat, fertile plain; behind them to the west, distant mountains. Wide horizon, autumn sun. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre.
shang-yang: 356 BCE, a market gate in Qin: by a tall wooden pole set up at the south gate of a rammed-earth town, a crowd of farmers and townspeople in hemp clothing watches as an official in robes hands a pile of bronze coins to a man who carried the pole; nearby clerks read bamboo-slip edicts; fields with farmers ploughing beyond the wall. Figures small, daylight. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
guiling: 354 BCE, Guiling on the North China plain: a Qi army waits in ambush in a wooded ravine beside a road, soldiers with crossbows and dagger-axes crouched behind trees; along the road a long, tired Wei column of chariots and infantry hurries home from the siege of Handan, unaware. A strategist in a light carriage watches from the hillside, small and from behind. Late afternoon. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre.
qin-bashu: 316 BCE, the Sichuan basin near Chengdu: a Qin army in iron-and-leather armour with crossbows and dagger-axes marches down from steep forested mountain passes along a plank road built into the cliffs, emerging onto a lush green plain of rice fields, rivers and bamboo; a walled town in the distance. Mist on the mountains, small figures. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art, green and ochre.
hu-fu: 307 BCE, Handan in Zhao: on a training ground outside the city walls, soldiers in close-fitting tunics, trousers, belts and boots in steppe style ride small horses bareback or on saddle cloths with no stirrups, shooting bows at targets while galloping; older soldiers in long robes and chariots stand aside watching. A king in the new dress, small and from behind, observes. Dust, northern hills. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre.
zhao-zhongshan: 296 BCE, Lingshou in Zhongshan at the foot of the Taihang mountains: Zhao horsemen without stirrups and infantry with banners approach the walled city from the plain, while inside the walls tall tiered tomb mounds and palace terraces rise; townspeople leave by a gate with carts. Seen from a mountain slope far off, small figures, thin haze. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
qi-song: 286 BCE, Shangqiu, capital of Song: a Qi army of chariots, crossbowmen and infantry with dagger-axes marches past canal-side markets and fields into the gates of a rich walled city; merchants' boats on the canal, carts of grain, townspeople watching from the walls. Seen from a distance, flat plain, clear day. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre on a pale ground.
yue-yi: 284 BCE, Linzi in Qi: allied armies under many different coloured banners encamp across a wide plain before the great rammed-earth walls of the Qi capital, chariots and infantry with dagger-axes in long lines, smoke from campfires drifting over the fields. Figures small, no wounds shown. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art. One single unified scene, no inset or panels.
qu-yuan: 278 BCE, the Miluo River in southern Chu: a lone gaunt poet in a long robe and tall hat, seen small and from behind, stands on a rocky riverbank among reeds and orchids, gazing at the swift river under grey clouds; a fisherman in a small boat drifts nearby, autumn mist on wooded hills. Quiet and melancholy, nothing violent. Ink and colour on silk in the manner of a Chu silk painting, flowing lines, black, cinnabar and ochre.
changping: 260 BCE, Changping in the hills of southern Shanxi: seen from a high ridge, a vast Qin army has encircled the Zhao camp in a valley, long earthen ramparts and stockades on both sides, banners on every hill, smoke from cooking fires; tiny columns of soldiers in leather armour move between forts. No combat close up, only the scale of the siege under a cold sky. Bronze-age lacquer painting palette, black, cinnabar and ochre.
qin-han: 230 BCE, Xinzheng: Qin soldiers in iron and leather armour with crossbows and long halberds march in disciplined ranks through the opened gate of the walled Han capital; Han court officials in robes kneel at the roadside presenting bronze seals and maps on trays; townspeople watch from rooftops. Seen from a distance, clear morning. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, with Qin-period details.
qin-zhao: 228 BCE, Handan: Qin troops in iron-and-leather armour with crossbows stream across the plain to the walls of the Zhao capital, banners raised over the gate towers; a covered carriage under guard leaves the city, while in the far north mountains a small band of riders escapes toward Dai. Figures small, winter light, no fighting close up. Ink and colour on aged silk in the manner of early Chinese pictorial art.
jing-ke: 227 BCE, the palace at Xianyang: a vast Qin audience hall of black-lacquered pillars on a high rammed-earth terrace; a man in a plain robe kneels before the throne platform, unrolling a long map scroll on a wooden roller, the glint of a dagger revealed at its end; courtiers in black robes recoil, guards stand at the foot of the steps. Figures small and seen from the side, no faces in detail. Han tomb mural style, black and red on plaster.
qin-wei: 225 BCE, Daliang: seen from a distant embankment, Qin labourers and soldiers have cut dykes so channels from the Yellow River pour toward the walled city; floodwater surrounds the walls, part of the wall has slumped into the water, small boats float among the rooftops; Qin camps on higher ground. Grey rainy sky, muddy brown water. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, ink on paper.
qin-chu: 223 BCE, Shouchun in the Huai River country: a huge Qin army in dark armour with crossbows and halberds spreads across lowland fields and lakes toward the walled Chu capital, with supply carts and camps stretching to the horizon; Chu banners of red over the walls; reed marshes and rivers. Seen from far away, many tiny figures, overcast light. Han tomb mural style, black, red and ochre on plaster.
qin-yan: 222 BCE, Liaodong: Qin horsemen without stirrups and infantry in winter clothing advance across a snowy northeastern plain toward a small walled town by the sea; a small Yan court group in fur-trimmed robes is led out of the gate under escort, carts loaded with bronzes. Pine forests, frozen river, pale winter sky. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style with pale wash.
great-wall-qin: 215 BCE, Jiuyuan on the Yellow River bend: thousands of conscript labourers in hemp tunics build a long rammed-earth wall across rolling grassland and ochre hills, pounding earth between wooden frames, carrying baskets on poles; watchtowers and beacon platforms along the ridge, Qin soldiers in armour guarding; supply carts and camps below, steppe stretching north. Wide panorama, dusty light. Han tomb mural style, earth reds and ochres on plaster.
lingqu: 214 BCE, Xing'an in Guangxi: a narrow canal winds between green karst peaks, a stone-faced spillway weir dividing the river into two channels; Qin workers in hemp tunics lay stone blocks and lock gates, flat-bottomed boats loaded with grain sacks are poled upstream; soldiers on the bank. Misty limestone hills, bamboo and rice fields. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, with light green wash.
book-burning: 213 BCE, Xianyang: in a large courtyard before government halls with black-lacquered pillars, Qin officials in black robes supervise clerks throwing bundles of bamboo-slip books onto a bonfire; carts deliver more bundles, scholars in robes stand far back in silence; smoke rises over the tiled roofs of the capital. Figures small, no violence to people. Han tomb mural style, black, red and ochre on plaster.
dazexiang: 209 BCE, Dazexiang in the rain: a band of about nine hundred conscripts in ragged hemp tunics gather in a muddy camp on a flooded plain, rain sheeting down, a rough banner made from cloth tied to a bamboo pole raised above them, men holding sticks and farm tools; the road ahead flooded, a small village of thatched huts. Seen from a distance. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, grey ink with rain texture.
julu: 207 BCE, Julu on the north China plain: seen from far away, an army has crossed a river and left its boats sunk and cooking pots broken on the bank; its troops charge toward a large encircling Qin camp with walls of earth, while allied armies watch from their own camps on hills. Dust, banners, small figures, no wounds, burning cooking pots in the foreground as a symbol. Han tomb mural style, earth colours on plaster.
hongmen: 206 BCE, Hongmen near Xianyang: a military tent pavilion with a raised floor, guests seated on mats at low lacquered tables with bronze wine vessels, a host and guest seated on separate sides; in the centre a man performs a sword dance while another rises to shield the guest; guards at the tent entrance. Figures small, faces not detailed, lamplight. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, the banquet scene typical of Han tomb carvings.
gaixia: 202 BCE, Gaixia at night: a small army camp encircled by vast enemy camps on a snowy plain, campfires all around the horizon; inside a tent, a lone general in armour sits with a woman and a black horse tethered nearby, listening to songs from the surrounding camps. Seen from outside and at a distance, figures small, melancholy mood, no violence. Han tomb mural style, dark ground with red and white figures.
baideng: 200 BCE, Baideng hill near Pingcheng: a small Han army in red-trimmed armour holds a snowy hilltop, surrounded on all sides by masses of Xiongnu horsemen in fur hats and coats, mounted without stirrups, their horses grouped by colour; winter steppe, low grey sky; an envoy with gifts walks down the slope. Seen from far away, many small figures. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, with pale wash.
zhang-qian: 138 BCE, the road west from Chang'an: a Han envoy carrying a tall staff of office with yak-tail tassels leads a small caravan of horses and a few attendants across a desert edge, the Tianshan snow peaks to the north, poplars and an oasis town with mud-brick walls ahead; a camel train of foreign merchants passes in the distance. Figures small, clear dry light. Han tomb mural style, ochre ground, red and black lines.
mobei: 119 BCE, north of the Gobi: a vast Han cavalry army in armour, riding without stirrups, with supply wagons arranged in a defensive ring, advances across a gravel steppe in a raging sandstorm; on the far horizon Xiongnu horsemen withdraw northward toward mountains. Seen from far away, tiny figures, swirling sand, no wounds. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style, with galloping horses in silhouette like Han relief carvings.
nanyue: 111 BCE, Panyu on the Pearl River: Han river ships with oars and tall towered decks and soldiers in armour come down the river toward a walled southern city among banyan trees and hills; fires burn on the city's edge at dusk, townspeople in short tunics watch from boats. Seen from across the water, small figures, humid haze. Han tomb mural style, earth reds, black and green on plaster.
shiji: c. 91 BCE, Chang'an: a quiet study in a Han timber house, a middle-aged scholar in a plain robe and cap, seen from behind, kneels at a low table writing on bamboo slips with a brush, bundles of bound bamboo-slip scrolls stacked around him, an oil lamp burning; through the open lattice the tiled roofs of the capital at night. No legible writing. Han tomb mural style, warm lamplit tones on plaster.
western-regions: 60 BCE, Wulei near Luntai: a Han garrison fort of rammed earth with a watchtower stands in an oasis at the edge of the Taklamakan desert; Han officials in robes and caps receive envoys from oasis kingdoms in felt hats and long coats bringing horses and camels; poplar trees, irrigated fields, the Tianshan mountains white with snow behind. Figures small, bright clear light. Han tomb mural style, ochre ground with red and black lines.
zhaojun: 33 BCE, the northern frontier near Hohhot: a young Han palace lady in a red cloak with a fur hood rides a horse at the head of a small procession, holding a pipa, followed by attendants, carts and an escort of Xiongnu horsemen in fur hats; the green steppe opens out ahead with felt tents and herds, mountains behind. Figures small, seen from the side, autumn wind. Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing style with soft colour wash.
wang-mang: 9 CE, Chang'an: in the courtyard of the Weiyang palace, with tiled-roof halls on high platforms, officials in robes and caps kneel in long rows before a hall as a new ruler, small and seen from behind, ascends the steps; in the foreground clerks lay out new bronze coins of unusual knife and spade shapes on trays and a land survey map. Formal, calm, overcast morning. Han tomb mural style, black, red and ochre on plaster.
lulin: 17 CE, the forested Lülin mountains of Hubei: ragged famine refugees in patched hemp tunics and straw sandals gather in a hidden valley camp among steep wooded hills, hundreds of small figures sharing thin millet gruel from iron pots, sharpening farm tools and bamboo spears, a few with simple bows; thatched lean-to shelters, cooking smoke rising into grey autumn mist, a parched terraced plain visible far below. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, earthy ochres and soft reds on plaster, loose brushwork, flaking surface.
kunyang: 23 CE, outside the walled town of Kunyang in Henan: a vast imperial army camp with banners and war chariots lies scattered in a violent thunderstorm, tents collapsing and horses bolting, while a small band of horsemen without stirrups charges from a gate in the rammed-earth wall; a swollen river in the foreground, figures fleeing small and distant, lightning over the plain. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on pale paper, flat stylised horses and chariots in horizontal registers.
guangwu: 25 CE, Luoyang: a new Eastern Han court assembles in a great timber hall with hipped tiled roofs on a rammed-earth terrace, ministers in black robes and tall jinxian caps kneeling in long rows on mats, a small seated emperor far away beneath a canopy; carts loaded with archives and bronze vessels arrive through the gate, the Luo River and city walls behind in clear morning light. Painted as a Han tomb mural, mineral red, black and ochre on whitewashed plaster, outlined figures in procession.
white-horse: 68 CE, outside Luoyang: two Indian monks in saffron robes walk beside a white horse laden with bundles of palm-leaf sutras wrapped in cloth, approaching a modest walled compound with Han-style tiled gate towers and a courtyard hall; Han officials in dark robes and caps greet them at the gate, poplars and wheat fields around, the city wall faint in the distance in soft afternoon light. Painted in Han tomb-mural style, warm earth pigments on plaster, simple confident outlines, quiet devotional mood.
ban-chao: 73 CE, the oasis of Shule (Kashgar) in the Tarim Basin: a small Han detachment of a few dozen soldiers in lamellar armour and red-bordered tunics, horses without stirrups, rides beside local oasis allies in felt caps and woollen coats toward a mud-brick walled town with poplar trees and irrigated fields; camels and a caravan nearby, the snowy Pamir peaks rising beyond a sandy plain under a pale sky. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, flat silhouetted riders in a horizontal frieze.
cai-lun: 105 CE, a workshop near the Luoyang palace: labourers in hemp tunics pound mulberry bark, hemp and rags in stone mortars, soak pulp in large vats, lift thin sheets on bamboo screens and lay them to dry against a sunny wall; in the courtyard beyond, a court official in dark robe and cap presents a neat stack of pale sheets to seated officials under a tiled eave. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural depicting daily labour, ochre, black and red on plaster, lively small figures.
zhang-heng: 132 CE, the observatory court at Luoyang: a large bronze urn-shaped instrument stands in a timber hall, eight bronze dragons around its body each holding a ball above an open-mouthed bronze toad below; one ball has just dropped into a toad's mouth while scholars in dark Han robes and caps lean close to look, an armillary sphere and bamboo-slip records nearby, lattice light falling on the floor. Painted as a Han tomb mural, black outline with cinnabar and ochre washes on plaster, calm instructional composition.
yellow-turbans: 184 CE, the plain of Julu in Hebei: thousands of peasants with yellow cloth headbands gather in a great crowd before a simple earthen altar where a Daoist leader, tiny in the distance, raises a staff; yellow banners without writing flutter, farm tools and spears held aloft, villages and bare winter fields stretching to the horizon, smoke rising from a far county town. Painted in the style of an Eastern Han tomb mural, yellow ochre, black and red on cracked plaster, crowds rendered as rhythmic repeated figures.
guandu: 200 CE, Guandu on the Henan plain: at night, flames and smoke rise from a vast enemy supply depot of grain carts and storehouses at Wuchao, seen from a distance, while lines of cavalry without stirrups and foot soldiers with halberds and wooden shields move across the flat land; earthwork ramparts and watchtowers of two opposing camps face each other across the plain. Rendered as a Han pictorial stone-relief rubbing, black ink on paper, stylised horses and fire in flat registers.
red-cliffs: 208 CE, Chibi on the Yangtze: on a wide river at dusk, a great fleet of linked wooden warships with matting sails burns as small fire boats driven by a southeast wind sail into it; red cliffs on the southern bank, opposing ships and soldiers watching from a distance, smoke and orange glow reflected in dark water, no individual faces. Painted in the style of a late Han tomb mural, cinnabar, black and ochre washes on plaster, sweeping rhythmic brushwork.
cao-pi: 220 CE, a raised abdication altar near Luoyang: on a broad earthen terrace with steps, ministers and generals in black court robes and tall caps stand in ranks while a small figure ascends to receive a jade seal from another in imperial robes, ceremonial banners and bronze ritual vessels around, tiled Han-style halls and city walls in the distance under a pale winter sky. Painted as a Han tomb mural, black outlines with muted red and ochre, solemn stately procession of small figures.
shu-han: 221 CE, Chengdu in the Sichuan basin: a coronation ceremony on an altar south of the city, a small crowned figure in black and red imperial robes seen from behind facing heaven, officials in caps and long robes lined in rows, a slender robed chancellor standing nearby; red banners, bronze tripods with incense smoke, green hills and the walled city beyond in humid spring light. Rendered in Han pictorial brick relief style from Sichuan tombs, warm grey clay texture with ink-rubbing tones and touches of red.
yiling: 222 CE, the Yangtze gorges near Yiling: a chain of dozens of timber stockade camps stretches for miles along wooded riverbanks and hills, set ablaze in a summer night as fire leaps from camp to camp; smoke billows over the gorge, distant troops withdraw along a mountain path, boats on the dark river. Painted in the style of a late Han tomb mural, cinnabar and ochre flames on black and grey, rhythmic repeated tents and mountains, no close figures.
wuzhang: 234 CE, Wuzhang Plains in Shaanxi: a large army camp of tents and wooden palisades on a high loess terrace above the Wei River on an autumn night, a single lamp glowing in the main command tent, banners hanging still; a large falling star crosses the dark sky above, sentries small and quiet at the gates, the opposing camp's fires faint across the river. Painted in Han-Jin tomb-mural style, deep indigo night with ochre and cinnabar accents on plaster, melancholy stillness.
wei-shu: 263 CE, the mountains of Yinping and the walls of Chengdu: soldiers wrapped in felt blankets roll and climb down steep forested cliffs on a narrow hidden route, ropes and plank paths on the rock face; far below, on the Chengdu plain, a city gate opens and a small procession in white robes with a bound carriage comes out to surrender before a waiting army. Painted in Han-Jin tomb-mural style, earth reds, greens and ochre, dramatic vertical mountains with tiny figures.
jin-founded: 266 CE, Luoyang: an enthronement in the palace audience hall, a tiled timber hall raised on a stone platform with red pillars, officials of the Sima court in wide-sleeved robes and lacquered gauze caps bowing in rows across a broad courtyard, a small seated figure on the throne far in the distance; banners, bronze incense burners and drums, early spring light. Painted in the style of a Gu Kaizhi handscroll, fine gossamer lines, delicate mineral colours on aged silk.
jin-wu: 280 CE, Jianye on the Yangtze: a great fleet of multi-deck timber tower ships with matting sails descends the broad river, iron chains strung across the water by the defenders melted and broken by burning rafts; on the shore, the walled southern capital opens its gates, a small procession of figures in plain robes coming out to surrender, green hills and morning mist. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, fine continuous lines, soft mineral colour on silk.
eight-princes: 291 CE, Luoyang: a wide view of the capital's palace district at dusk, rival bands of armoured soldiers with banners of different colours marching through broad avenues between walled compounds, palace gates shut, smoke rising from a burning mansion in the distance, frightened townspeople small along the walls; tiled roofs, watchtowers and the city wall under a heavy grey sky. Painted in the style of a Western Jin tomb brick painting, quick ink lines with ochre and red washes on pale clay.
yongjia: 311 CE, Luoyang: smoke rising over the burning walled capital seen from a distant hillside, Xiongnu horsemen in fur caps and belted coats on the plain before the gates; in the foreground, long columns of refugee families with ox carts, bundles and children trudging south along a dusty road through bare fields, a few scholars carrying boxes of scrolls. Painted in the style of a Six Dynasties handscroll, fine gossamer line, muted ochre and grey tones on aged silk.
eastern-jin: 317 CE, Jiankang on the lower Yangtze: refugee northern gentry in wide-sleeved robes arrive by boat at a riverside city of timber halls and tiled roofs surrounded by green hills and lakes; in the palace courtyard officials gather before a modest hall to honour a new ruler, small in the distance, while porters unload chests and scrolls from boats at the quay in warm hazy southern light. Painted in the style of Gu Kaizhi's handscrolls, fine line, soft mineral blues and greens on silk.
lanting: 353 CE, the Orchid Pavilion near Shaoxing: in a spring bamboo grove, scholars in loose robes and gauze caps sit along the banks of a winding stream, lacquer wine cups floating down the water toward them; a small open pavilion with a tiled roof, one figure seen from behind writing at a low table, wooded hills and clear sky beyond. Painted as a Six Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, fine gossamer lines, pale greens and ochres on aged silk, gentle relaxed mood.
mogao: 366 CE, Dunhuang: a lone monk in a patched robe with a staff stands at the foot of a long sandstone cliff along a dry river valley at sunset, the cliff glowing gold as if lit by a thousand lights; a few workers with picks begin to carve a small cave entrance in the rock face, poplar trees, sand dunes and the oasis far off. Painted in the style of an early Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, mineral greens and blues, rough flaking pigment texture.
fei-river: 383 CE, the Fei River in Anhui: a vast northern army of armoured cavalry with stirrups and long lances and infantry with banners crowds the north bank and begins to fall back in disorder, while a smaller southern army in lamellar armour wades across the shallow river toward them; the Bagong mountain in the distance with its trees mistaken for soldiers, dust clouds over the plain, figures small. Painted in the style of a Six Dynasties handscroll, fine line, earthy ochre and grey with touches of red on silk.
liu-song: 420 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a palace courtyard by the Qinhuai river, a ceremony in which officials in wide-sleeved robes and lacquered gauze caps line a stone stair while a tall general in armour and robes, small and seen from behind, ascends toward the throne hall; banners, guards with halberds, green Purple Mountain and city walls beyond in soft southern light. Painted in the manner of a Southern Dynasties handscroll, fine gossamer line, muted mineral colours on aged silk.
wei-unifies-north: 439 CE, Gansu corridor approaching Guzang (Wuwei): long columns of Xianbei Tuoba cavalry in hooded caps and armour, riding with stirrups, cross a dry steppe plain toward a walled oasis city of rammed earth beneath the snowy Qilian mountains; camels and baggage carts follow, banners streaming, the city gate open as small figures come out to submit. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei tomb mural, bold ink outlines with red and ochre washes, energetic horses.
yungang: 460 CE, Yungang near Pingcheng (Datong): a long sandstone cliff where hundreds of workers on timber scaffolding carve a colossal seated Buddha with broad shoulders and a calm smiling face in a huge niche; monks in robes and Xianbei officials in hooded caps watch from below, chisels and baskets of stone, a river and dry yellow hills under clear sky. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei cave mural, mineral blues, greens and ochre, flat stylised figures with flaking pigment.
southern-qi: 479 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a palace of tiled timber halls beside the Qinhuai river where a young emperor in robes, small and distant, leaves the palace by carriage under escort, while officials in wide-sleeved robes and gauze caps wait in rows to receive a new ruler at the throne hall; willows along the canal, Purple Mountain behind, a quiet overcast sky. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties handscroll, fine line, pale mineral colours on aged silk.
xiaowen: 494 CE, Luoyang: a long procession of the Xianbei court arrives at the rebuilt capital, nobles changing from tight-sleeved hooded steppe coats into wide-sleeved Chinese robes and caps, ox carriages and baggage trains passing through a great gate; new tiled halls and pagodas under construction, and far off along the Yi River, small workers beginning to carve cave niches into limestone cliffs. Painted in the style of the Northern Wei imperial procession reliefs of Longmen, carved stone texture with soft added colour.
liang-founded: 502 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a lakeside southern capital filled with Buddhist temples and tall wooden pagodas, monks in robes chanting in a temple courtyard while courtiers in wide-sleeved robes and gauze caps gather at a palace hall; willows, misty Purple Mountain, painted boats on the Qinhuai river, incense smoke rising in calm spring light. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties handscroll in the manner of Gu Kaizhi, fine gossamer line, soft mineral greens and reds on silk.
zhongli: 507 CE, Zhongli on the Huai River: a long timber pontoon bridge across the flooded river burns as southern warships with matting sails ram it during spring floods, while a huge northern camp on the far bank lies cut off; cavalry with stirrups and infantry seen small in the distance, smoke over brown water, willow banks and flat fields. Painted in the style of a Six Dynasties handscroll, fine line, muted ochre, grey and red on aged silk.
six-garrisons: 524 CE, Wuchuan on the northern frontier: on a windswept grassland plateau, a mud-walled garrison fort is surrounded by restless frontier soldiers in fur-lined Xianbei coats and hooded caps, mounted with stirrups, gathering with bows and lances; yurts and herds of horses nearby, a lone beacon tower, the Yin mountains behind under a cold grey sky. Painted in the style of a Northern Wei tomb mural, bold black outlines, ochre and red washes on plaster, sweeping horses.
wei-splits: 534 CE, the north China plain: two long caravans of court carriages, soldiers and banners move away from each other in opposite directions across a wide landscape, one heading east toward the walled city of Ye beside the Zhang river, the other west through the mountain passes toward Chang'an; people in Xianbei and Chinese dress, carts loaded with archives, pale autumn light. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural, lively ink outlines with red and ochre washes, many small figures.
ly-bi: 544 CE, Jiaozhi in the Red River delta near present-day Hanoi: a lowland citadel of earthen walls and timber halls surrounded by rice paddies and canals, local people in simple wrapped garments gathered in a great crowd as a leader, small and seen from behind, stands on a raised platform; war boats on the river, banana palms and limestone hills on the horizon, humid golden afternoon. Painted as a Six Dynasties-style handscroll, fine line, soft greens and ochres on aged silk.
hou-jing: 548 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): the walled palace city under siege seen from a distant hill, tall siege towers and earthen mounds pressed against the walls, smoke rising from burned temples and mansions, the Qinhuai river choked with abandoned boats; small soldiers on the walls, an empty overgrown palace garden in the foreground under a grey winter sky. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties handscroll, fine gossamer line, muted grey and ochre on aged silk, sombre mood.
northern-qi: 550 CE, Ye in Hebei: a grand enthronement in a palace courtyard with tiled halls and tall pillars, Xianbei nobles and officials in tight-sleeved riding coats and Chinese robes kneeling in rows, a young ruler small on the dais; mounted guards with stirrups, banners, horses in caparisons, the Zhang river and city walls beyond. Painted in the style of a Northern Qi tomb mural such as those of Lou Rui, vivid ink outlines, red, ochre and green washes on plaster, lively horses.
jiangling-falls: 554 CE, Jiangling on the middle Yangtze: winter, smoke rises from a palace building where great piles of scroll bundles are burning, seen from a distance across the walled city; beyond the gates, long columns of captive townspeople with bundles walk north escorted by northern cavalry with stirrups through bare fields, the wide river grey behind. Painted in the style of a Six Dynasties handscroll, fine gossamer line, ash grey, ochre and faint red on aged silk, sorrowful mood.
chen-founded: 557 CE, Jiankang (Nanjing): a modest palace courtyard partly rebuilt after war, scaffolding on damaged halls, officials in wide-sleeved robes and gauze caps gathered before a veteran general, small and seen from behind, climbing the steps of the throne hall; soldiers in lamellar armour, ruined walls being repaired, the Yangtze and Purple Mountain behind under hazy light. Painted in the style of a Southern Dynasties handscroll, fine line, pale mineral colours on silk.
northern-zhou: 557 CE, Chang'an in the Wei River valley: a ceremonial enthronement at the Western Wei palace, officials and Xianbei generals in tight-sleeved coats and caps lined up in a broad courtyard with banners and drums, a young ruler small and distant on a raised platform; mounted guards with stirrups, rammed-earth walls, loess hills beyond in clear winter air. Painted in the style of a Northern Zhou tomb mural, bold black outline, red and ochre on plaster, simple stately composition.
zhou-conquers-qi: 577 CE, Ye in Hebei: a large Northern Zhou army of armoured cavalry with stirrups and lances and infantry with banners enters the opened gates of a walled capital in winter, townspeople watching from the walls, palace halls and Buddhist pagodas inside; snow on the plain, the army stretching back to the horizon. Painted in the style of a Northern Zhou tomb mural, bold ink outlines with red and ochre washes, rhythmic files of horses.
sui-founded: 581 CE, the Chang'an region: a vast new capital laid out on a grid on open land southeast of the old city, workers raising rammed-earth walls and broad avenues, surveyors with measuring rods, timber palace halls on a terrace; in the foreground, officials in round-collar robes and soft black caps watch a small figure inspecting the plans, Zhongnan mountains on the horizon. Painted in the style of a Sui-Tang court painting, fine line, mineral blues and greens with ochre.
sui-conquers-chen: 589 CE, the Yangtze at Jiankang (Nanjing): at dawn, a great fleet of multi-deck Sui warships with matting sails crosses the broad river from the north bank, troops landing on the southern shore; the walled southern capital beyond with tiled halls and pagodas, Purple Mountain behind, small figures of defenders and the surrender procession far off, mist on the water. Painted in the style of a Sui dynasty cave mural from Dunhuang, mineral blues and greens, ochre ground, many small figures.
grand-canal: 605 CE, near Luoyang: tens of thousands of conscript labourers in hemp tunics dig a broad straight canal across the flat plain, carrying earth in baskets on shoulder poles, building willow-lined embankments; officials in round-collar robes supervise from horseback, a few grain barges already floating on a finished stretch, the city and hills faint in hazy morning light. Painted in the style of a Sui-Tang Dunhuang mural, mineral greens and ochres, many tiny figures in rhythmic rows.
keju: 605 CE, an examination hall in Luoyang: rows of candidates in plain round-collar robes and black soft caps kneel at low tables writing with brushes on paper scrolls, ink stones beside them, inside a long timber hall with lattice windows; officials in red and purple robes walk the aisles as proctors, a courtyard with pines outside in morning light, the written pages shown only as blank pale sheets. Painted in Tang court painting style, fine line, mineral colours on silk.
goguryeo-campaign: 612 CE, the Salsu River (Cheongcheon) in northern Korea: a huge army retreating across a wide shallow river in late summer, distant soldiers in lamellar armour struggling through the current as a sudden rush of water from upstream sweeps the crossing; Goguryeo mountain fortresses on forested ridges above, archers on the heights, horses and banners small in the distance. Painted in the style of a Goguryeo tomb mural, bold outlines, red ochre and black on plaster, energetic stylised horses.
tang-founded: 618 CE, Chang'an: in the Daxing palace, a great timber hall with red pillars and grey tiled roof on a stone platform, officials in round-collar robes and black futou caps bowing in rows across a vast courtyard while a small figure in yellow robes, seen from behind, takes the throne; guards with halberds, banners, bronze incense burners, clear spring sky. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Yan Liben, fine line, rich mineral reds, blues and greens on silk.
xuanwu-gate: 626 CE, Chang'an: dawn at the Xuanwu Gate on the northern side of the palace city, a massive rammed-earth gate with a timber gate tower, its doors half open; armoured guards with stirruped horses and halberds waiting tensely in the shadow of the wall, a few riders approaching along an empty avenue, willow trees and the palace roofs beyond in early grey light, scene seen from a distance. Painted in Tang court painting style, fine line, muted mineral blues and greens on silk.
eastern-turks: 630 CE, the Yinshan mountains: a Tang cavalry force with stirrups, lamellar armour and red banners rides out of a snowy dawn mist toward a vast Turkic camp of felt yurts and horse herds on the steppe; Turkic horsemen in long braided hair and belted kaftans scatter, captured herds in the foreground, distant mountains white with snow. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues, greens and white on ochre ground, galloping horses.
anxi: 640 CE, Gaochang near Turpan: a Tang army with stirruped cavalry, lamellar armour and banners approaches a large mud-brick oasis city with thick walls and Buddhist stupas, the Flaming Mountains glowing red behind; vineyards, irrigation channels and poplars in the foreground, camels and supply carts, townspeople in Central Asian dress watching from the walls under a hot pale sky. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, mineral greens and blues, flaking pigment texture.
wencheng: 641 CE, approaching Rasa (Lhasa): a long Tang bridal caravan crosses a high Tibetan valley, a covered carriage and horses carrying a princess and her attendants in Tang high-waisted dresses, followed by porters with chests, scrolls, seeds and a Buddha statue on a cart; Tibetan riders in fur-trimmed robes come to welcome them, snowy peaks, prayer cairns and a hill fortress in the distance. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Yan Liben, mineral blues and greens on silk, fine line.
baekgang: 663 CE, the mouth of the Geum River in Korea: on a wide estuary, a fleet of large Tang warships with matting sails and rows of oars forms a battle line as smaller Japanese and Baekje boats burn, smoke drifting across the water; hills and a coastal fortress on the shore, scene viewed from a distance, small figures on decks. Painted in the style of a Tang Dunhuang mural, mineral blues and greens on ochre ground, stylised waves and flames.
wu-zetian: 690 CE, Luoyang (Shendu): the Mingtang of Empress Wu, a towering three-storey square timber hall with dark grey tiled roofs, red columns and broad eaves, its top storey capped by a round roof with a gilded phoenix finial, rising above walled palace courts; a grand assembly of officials in red and purple round-collar robes and black futou caps bowing in a vast courtyard, court ladies in high-waisted gowns, banners, a small seated figure far away on a raised throne. Not the Ming-Qing Temple of Heaven: no blue roofs, no white marble terraces. Painted in Tang court painting style in the manner of Zhang Xuan, mineral reds, golds and greens on silk. A single unified picture.
poyang: 1363, Lake Poyang in Jiangxi: a vast summer lake under a hazy sky, hundreds of war junks with batten sails and tall multi-deck tower ships locked in battle; small fire-ships drift downwind toward the large enemy vessels, plumes of smoke rising over the water, distant green hills and reed banks on the shore, tiny armoured figures with spears and bows on the decks seen from afar. Painted as a Yuan-to-early-Ming handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, sweeping horizontal composition, misty water rendered in fine wave lines.
ming-founded: 1368, Nanjing: a grand ceremony before a newly built palace hall of red pillars and yellow-tiled hipped roofs beneath Zhongshan's green slopes; rows of officials in early Ming round-collared robes and black gauze caps kneel in a stone courtyard, banners and parasols lining the approach, the new emperor a small distant figure on the terrace, massive city walls of grey brick beyond. Painted in the style of a Ming court painting, mineral colours on silk, orderly symmetrical composition, clear morning light.
haijin-maritime-ban: 1371, a Fujian coastal harbour: tall-sterned junks lie beached and idle on a quiet tidal shore, their sails furled, while Ming soldiers in red-padded coats and helmets patrol a stone watchtower on the headland; fishermen mend nets by thatched houses, and far out at sea a single official tribute ship with large lug sails passes under escort. Rendered as a Ming woodblock-print illustration with hand-applied colour, crisp black outlines, calm grey sea and pale sky.
jingnan: 1402, Nanjing: a great army approaches the towering grey-brick walls and the vast Jubao gate of the Ming southern capital, columns of cavalry and infantry in lamellar armour under red banners crossing a river plain; the city gate stands open, smoke drifts from a palace district within, and riverboats crowd the Qinhuai waterway. Figures small, seen from a high viewpoint at late afternoon. Painted as a Ming blue-green landscape hanging scroll, mineral azurite and malachite tones, fine ink outlines.
beijing-capital: 1421, Beijing: the newly completed Forbidden City seen from a high vantage at dawn, golden-yellow glazed roofs of the great halls rising above vermilion walls and white marble terraces, a moat and corner towers, wide courtyards where officials in red and blue robes assemble in tiny rows; scaffolding and timber stacks from the builders still visible at the edges, the Western Hills faint on the horizon. Painted in the manner of a Ming court painting of palace architecture, ink and colour on silk, precise ruled-line detail.
tumu: 1449, Tumu near the northern frontier: a dry upland plain at dusk below brown hills and a distant stretch of rammed-earth wall, a Ming army camp of white tents and wagons in disarray, Oirat Mongol horsemen in fur hats and quilted coats sweeping in from the steppe with bows, dust clouds rising, abandoned banners on the ground; all figures small and distant, no bloodshed shown. Painted as a Ming ink-and-colour handscroll in the tradition of frontier battle scrolls, muted ochres and greys.
macau: 1557, Macau peninsula: a small rocky harbour with green hills where a Portuguese carrack with high castles and square sails lies at anchor beside Chinese junks; on the beach Portuguese traders in doublets and broad hats barter with Ming merchants in robes over bales of silk and porcelain, a few simple timber and mat-shed buildings and a modest wooden cross on a hill, sampans on the water. Rendered as a sixteenth-century Ming woodblock-print illustration with soft hand colouring, clear daylight.
zhang-juzheng-reforms: 1573, Beijing: inside a Ming grand secretariat hall with lattice windows and red columns, officials in crimson robes with rank badges and black gauze caps bend over tables piled with land registers, account books and abacuses, clerks carrying bundles of documents in and out; a senior minister seen from behind at a large desk, a boy emperor's yellow-curtained seat in the distance. Painted in Ming court-painting style, ink and mineral colour on silk, the pages shown as blank or blurred.
imjin: 1593, Pyongyang in winter: Ming armies in iron helmets and padded armour advance across a snowy plain toward the stone walls and pavilion-topped gates of the Korean city by the frozen Taedong River, cannon on wheeled carriages firing white smoke, Joseon soldiers in black brimmed hats alongside them, Japanese defenders small on the ramparts; scene viewed from a distance. Painted as a late-Ming hand-coloured woodblock illustration crossed with Korean folding-screen battle painting, ink with blue, red and ochre.
ricci: 1601, Beijing: in a Ming palace courtyard pavilion a European Jesuit in Chinese scholar's robes and square cap, seen from behind, presents gifts to eunuch officials in court dress: a gilded mechanical striking clock, a small clavichord and a large painted world map unrolled on a table; red lacquer columns, latticed doors and a glimpse of yellow roofs beyond. Painted in the manner of a Ming court painting, ink and colour on silk, soft afternoon light, the map shown with continents but no lettering.
later-jin: 1616, Hetu Ala in the Manchurian hills: a fortified hilltop town of wooden palisades and simple tiled halls among pine forests and river valleys; Jurchen warriors with shaved foreheads and queues, wearing fur-trimmed coats, assemble in eight great blocks under plain yellow, white, red and blue banners, some bordered, horses and archers in ranks; a leader stands small on a raised platform. Painted as a Qing-court-style hanging scroll of early Manchu history, ink and colour on silk, crisp autumn light.
sarhu: 1619, Sarhu in the Liaodong mountains: Jurchen cavalry under coloured banners charge down a forested slope through drifting snow toward a Ming encampment on a river plain, Ming musketeers and cannon producing white smoke, overturned carts and scattered pennants; mountains and dark firs frame the scene, all figures small at a distance, no gore. Painted in the style of an early Qing illustrated military chronicle, ink and light colour on paper, dynamic diagonal composition.
shanhai: 1644, Shanhai Pass where the Great Wall meets the Bohai Sea: the massive brick gate tower stands open as columns of Manchu banner cavalry with queues and fur-trimmed helmets ride through alongside Ming frontier troops; on the plain beyond, armies clash beneath a sudden dust storm, the sea glinting to the east and the wall snaking over the mountains. Figures small, seen from high above. Painted as a Qing court painting of a historic campaign, mineral colours on silk with fine detail.
koxinga: 1662, Fort Zeelandia near Tainan, Taiwan: a squat Dutch brick fortress with angled bastions on a sandbar beside a lagoon, encircled by a fleet of Chinese war junks with patterned sails and Ming loyalist soldiers in armour with banners camped on the shore; cannon smoke drifts over the walls, Dutch ships small at anchor offshore, palm trees and coastal plains around. Rendered in the manner of a seventeenth-century Dutch-Chinese engraved map view with watercolour wash, high bird's-eye perspective.
three-feudatories: 1673, Kunming in Yunnan: a walled southwestern city beside the blue Dian Lake with red-earth hills behind, rebel troops in Ming-style armour assemble under plain banners at the city gate while, far to the north across mountain ranges, columns of Qing bannermen with queues and conical hats march with supply carts; terraced fields and pines in between. Painted as a Kangxi-era Qing court landscape with campaign figures, blue-green palette on silk, panoramic composition.
taiwan-1683: 1683, the Penghu islands in the Taiwan Strait: a great Qing war fleet of hundreds of junks with ribbed sails and dragon-eye bows engages a smaller Zheng fleet among low windswept islets, cannon smoke drifting across a choppy blue-green sea, sails ablaze in the distance, stone-walled fishing villages on the shore; all sailors tiny. Painted as a Qing court painting of a naval victory in the Castiglione-influenced manner, gouache-like colour on silk with careful perspective of waves and ships.
nerchinsk: 1689, Nerchinsk by the Shilka River: on an open meadow between a small Russian log fort with an onion-domed wooden church and a camp of Qing tents, two delegations meet under a large canopy; Qing envoys in court robes with queues and plumed hats, Russian envoys in long kaftans and fur caps, two Jesuit interpreters in black robes between them; cavalry escorts wait at a distance among birch forest. Painted as a Qing court painting with Western perspective, soft colours on silk, late summer light.
qing-tibet: 1720, Lhasa: the white and red Potala Palace rises on its hill above the valley as a long column of Qing bannermen with queues and conical hats, together with Tibetan and Mongol escorts, enters with a procession of monks in maroon robes carrying parasols and banners around a young lama on horseback; whitewashed houses, prayer flags without writing, and snowy peaks under a deep blue sky. Painted in a blend of Qing court painting and Tibetan thangka palette, mineral colours, fine line.
dzungar: 1757, the Ili valley in Xinjiang: Qing armies of banner cavalry with queues, lances and matchlocks cross wide grasslands below the snow-capped Tianshan, felt yurts of a Dzungar camp abandoned on the plain, herds of horses scattering, distant smoke from a burning encampment; the scene observed from a ridge, figures small. Painted in the style of Giuseppe Castiglione's Qianlong conquest engravings, rendered as a fine monochrome copperplate-style image with delicate hatching.
macartney: 1793, Chengde Mountain Resort: a large Mongolian-style ceremonial tent among the imperial gardens and wooded hills, British envoys in powdered wigs, knee breeches and red or blue coats approach with gifts of a telescope, a planetarium globe and scientific instruments, while Qing officials in court robes with plumed hats and mandarin beads line the path; the elderly emperor's sedan chair carried in at a distance. Painted as a Qing court painting with European-influenced perspective, soft gouache colours, early morning light.
nanking: 1842, the Yangtze River off Nanjing: British warships and paddle steamers lie at anchor before the city's grey walls and Purple Mountain; aboard HMS Cornwallis, Qing commissioners in court robes and red-tasselled hats sit at a long table opposite British officers in naval uniform, seen at a distance through the open quarterdeck, sailors in the rigging. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, fine black-and-white hatching, documents on the table shown blank.
taiping: 1851, Jintian village in the hills of Guangxi: thousands of peasants and miners with long unbraided hair tied up in red headcloths gather on a valley floor below green karst hills, raising plain yellow and red banners, carrying spears and farm tools, a simple wooden stage with a leader seen small from behind; thatched villages and rice terraces around, morning mist. Rendered in the Dianshizhai Pictorial lithograph style, crisp black line with crowded figures and detailed landscape.
summer-palace: 1860, Yuanmingyuan outside Beijing: great columns of smoke rise from burning palace halls and European-style marble pavilions across a landscape of lakes, arched bridges and willow islands; small figures of British and French soldiers in red coats and blue kepis carry off crates and porcelain along a path in the foreground, distant hills faint through the haze. Rendered as a nineteenth-century illustrated newspaper engraving, black-and-white wood engraving with dramatic smoke and fine hatching.
self-strengthening: 1861, Anqing on the Yangtze: a new arsenal compound of brick sheds and chimneys by the riverbank, Chinese artisans in short jackets and queues working lathes, forging gun barrels and assembling a small steam engine, Qing officials in robes and official hats inspecting with a foreign adviser; a steamboat and sailing junks on the river beyond. Painted as a Canton export painting in gouache on paper, bright clear colours, many small industrious figures.
yalu: 1894, the Yellow Sea off the mouth of the Yalu River: steel ironclads and cruisers of the Beiyang Fleet with tall funnels and Qing dragon flags (no lettering) exchange fire with Japanese warships in line ahead, thick black coal smoke and white gun smoke over a grey sea, one Chinese ship listing and burning in the distance; scene at sea level from far away. Rendered in the style of a Dianshizhai Pictorial lithograph, black ink line with dense wave patterns.
treaty-of-shimonoseki: 1895, Shimonoseki, Japan: the Shunpanro inn on a hill overlooking the narrow Kanmon Strait, steamships and small sailing boats on the water below; inside a tatami room furnished with Western tables and chairs, an elderly Qing envoy in robes and official hat sits among his delegation across from Japanese statesmen in Western frock coats, all seen small from the doorway, papers on the table blank. Rendered as a Meiji-era-influenced nineteenth-century newspaper engraving, fine black-and-white line with light tint.
hundred-days: 1898, Beijing: in a hall of the Forbidden City with red columns and painted ceiling beams, a young emperor in yellow robes, seen from behind, receives a kneeling scholar-official in plain blue robe holding a memorial; stacks of Western-style books, a globe and a model steamship on a side table, eunuchs waiting at the doorway and a curtained screen behind. Rendered in the Dianshizhai Pictorial lithograph style, detailed black line with light hand colour, pages blank.
boxers: 1900, Beijing: a broad view over the Tartar City walls toward the Legation Quarter, Western-style buildings with sandbagged rooftops, smoke rising from burning houses nearby; in the dusty streets, groups of Boxers in red sashes and headbands with spears and swords, and later columns of foreign troops of several nations in khaki and blue marching through a great city gate. Figures small and distant, no bloodshed. Rendered as a 1900 illustrated newspaper engraving, black-and-white with fine hatching.
exam-abolished: 1905, Beijing: the vast Shuntian examination compound, row upon row of tiny brick cells along narrow lanes, now silent and empty under an autumn sky, a few elderly scholars in long gowns and queues walking slowly between them, weeds in the courtyards; beyond the wall a new Western-style school building with students in uniforms. Rendered as a Dianshizhai Pictorial-style lithograph illustration, fine black line with muted wash, quiet melancholy mood.
wuchang: 1911, Wuchang on the Yangtze: at night, New Army soldiers in Western-style khaki uniforms and peaked caps, many with queues cut, gather with rifles before a Qing government yamen, plain white armbands on their sleeves, lanterns and torches lighting the scene; across the river the lights of Hankou and steamboats, the Yellow Crane Tower silhouette on Snake Hill. Rendered as a late-Qing illustrated newspaper lithograph, black line with sparse red and ochre tints.
abdication: 1912, Beijing: the Hall of Mental Cultivation in the Forbidden City on a cold February day, a small boy emperor in a yellow robe seated beside an Empress Dowager seen from a distance, ministers in Qing court robes bowing as an official presents a scroll edict with no visible writing; outside, snow on yellow-tiled roofs and an empty courtyard. Rendered as a watercolour sketch in early Republican illustration style, muted greys, golds and vermilion, figures small.
cn-hongxian-monarchy: 1915, Beijing: the Temple of Heaven complex in winter, a ceremonial procession of officials in revived archaic-style robes and tall hats mixed with men in Western military uniforms moving along the white marble causeway toward the round blue-roofed hall, an armoured motorcar waiting at the gate; bare cypress trees and a pale sky. All figures small. Rendered as a Republican-era watercolour sketch with ink outlines, subdued ironic stillness, no writing.
cn-may-fourth-movement: 1919, Beijing: in front of the Tiananmen gate, thousands of students in long scholar gowns and Western suits with straw boaters and caps march along a broad dusty avenue holding plain white banners and paper flags with no legible writing; a few policemen at a distance, willow trees and the red gate tower behind, spring daylight. Rendered as a Republican-era woodcut print in the style of the Lu Xun woodcut movement, bold black-and-white carving with strong contrast.
cn-ccp-founded: 1921, South Lake in Jiaxing: a covered wooden pleasure boat with a red-brown roof floats on the misty lake among willows and lotus leaves, a few men in long gowns and suits seated inside under the canopy, seen from the shore at a distance; a stone bridge and low tiled houses on the far bank. Rendered as a neutral 1920s ink-and-watercolour sketch, soft greys and greens, small anonymous figures. One single unified scene, not split into panels.
cn-northern-expedition: 1926, Guangzhou: columns of soldiers of the National Revolutionary Army in grey-blue uniforms with peaked caps, rifles and puttees march out along the Pearl River bund past arcaded colonnaded shophouses, crowds watching from balconies, porters carrying supplies on poles, a steam launch on the river; plain blue-and-white flags without writing, bright southern sun. Rendered as a Republican-era Lu Xun-school woodcut print, black ink with a single red accent, figures small.
cn-long-march: 1934-35, the mountains of southwest China: a long thin column of soldiers in worn grey uniforms and puttees with packs, straw sandals and rifles winds along a narrow trail across a snowy mountain pass and down to a river crossed by an iron-chain suspension bridge, porters and pack mules among them; vast mist-filled valleys below. All figures tiny in the landscape. Rendered as a muted documentary watercolour, cool blues and greys, neutral tone.
cn-xian-incident: 1936, Xi'an in December: a frosty dawn at the Huaqing Hot Springs below Mount Li, pavilions with grey tiled roofs, soldiers in winter uniforms and fur caps moving up the bare wintry hillside, an automobile parked by the gate; in the distance the walls of Xi'an and a pale winter sky. Figures small, no faces. Rendered as a 1930s Republican-era woodcut print, black ink on rough paper, stark contrasts.
cn-civil-war: 1946-49, the North China plain: a wide wintry landscape with long columns of soldiers in padded cotton uniforms, horse-drawn carts and peasants pushing wheelbarrows of supplies moving across frozen fields toward a distant walled town, smoke rising on the horizon, bare poplar trees along the road. Figures small, no combat shown up close. Rendered as a muted documentary watercolour of the late 1940s, earthy browns and greys, neutral and quiet.
cn-retreat-to-taiwan: 1949, Keelung harbour in northern Taiwan: crowded troopships and freighters unloading at the quay under green hills and grey rain clouds, soldiers in khaki uniforms and civilian families with suitcases, bundles and children coming down the gangways, wooden crates stacked under tarpaulins on the dock, Japanese-era warehouses behind. Figures small, faces indistinct. Rendered as a muted documentary gouache illustration, damp blues and greys, quiet reflective mood.
cn-prc-founded: 1949, Beijing: the Tiananmen gate tower on an autumn day seen from far across the square, great red lanterns hanging from the eaves, a large crowd filling the open space before it, rows of soldiers and flags in the distance, tiny figures on the gate balcony; clear blue October sky. Rendered as a neutral documentary watercolour illustration, soft reds and greys, no writing or portraits, calm and wide.
cn-great-leap-forward: 1958, a village on the North China plain at night: dozens of small brick backyard furnaces glow orange in a farm courtyard and along the edges of fields, villagers in padded jackets feeding them with wood and broken iron pots, smoke drifting over unharvested grain in the background, a commune dining hall with a long tiled roof nearby. Figures small. Rendered as a muted documentary gouache illustration, dark blues and ember oranges, neutral tone.
cn-great-famine: 1959-61, rural Xinyang in Henan: a bleak late-winter landscape of bare cracked fields and stripped trees under a grey sky, a silent village of mud-brick houses with empty courtyards, an empty commune granary with open doors, a few thin distant figures walking along a dirt road with baskets. No people in close-up, no bodies. Rendered as a sombre muted watercolour illustration, washed greys and ochres, quiet and restrained.
cn-cultural-revolution: 1966, a railway station in northern China: on a long platform under a grey sky, young people in green caps and padded jackets with bedrolls and enamel mugs board a steam train bound for the countryside, families watching from a distance; station walls behind are covered with large paper sheets shown only as blurred illegible strokes. Figures small and anonymous, no violence. Rendered as a muted documentary woodcut print, black and grey with restrained tones. One single unified scene, not split into panels.
cn-reform-opening: 1978-80s, coastal southern China: a landscape in transition seen from a hillside, rice paddies and old village houses in the foreground giving way to new construction sites with cranes, half-built factory blocks and a busy small port with container ships; farmers with a hand tractor, workers in blue overalls cycling along a dirt road. Figures small, anonymous. Rendered as a neutral documentary watercolour illustration, bright soft colours, optimistic but understated.
cn-tiananmen-1989: 1989, Beijing: a calm wide view of Tiananmen Square at dawn in late spring, the vast pale paving stretching toward the gate tower and distant buildings, a scattering of bicycles and a few tents seen far away, morning haze and soft light, no identifiable people. Rendered as a quiet muted documentary watercolour, pale greys and blues, reflective stillness, no text, no signs, no portraits.
cn-hong-kong-handover: 1997, Hong Kong: Victoria Harbour on a rainy night, the curved glass convention centre on the Wan Chai waterfront lit up, fireworks bursting over the water, skyscrapers along the Hong Kong Island skyline glowing in the mist, a large white ship with lit decks leaving the harbour; crowds with umbrellas small along the promenade, no identifiable people. Rendered as a muted documentary gouache illustration, deep blues and reflections of coloured light, no lettering.
cn-wto-accession: 2001, Doha, Qatar: a modern conference centre by the turquoise Persian Gulf seen at dusk, palm trees and wide boulevards, delegates in suits small in the distance walking under a colonnade, flags of many nations without legible details on poles; and across the sea a suggestion of container cranes and stacked cargo boxes at a busy port. Rendered as a neutral documentary watercolour illustration, warm sand and turquoise tones, no text.
cn-beijing-olympics: 2008, Beijing: the steel lattice 'Bird's Nest' National Stadium glowing red and gold at night, fireworks bursting overhead in the summer sky, the blue bubble-clad Water Cube aquatics centre nearby, crowds of tiny spectators streaming across the wide plaza and along illuminated walkways lined with young trees. No identifiable people. Rendered as a lively but neutral documentary gouache illustration, saturated night colours, no logos, no lettering.
cn-covid-19-wuhan: 2019-20, Wuhan in winter: a wide view of deserted city streets and an empty multi-lane avenue beside the Yangtze, the Yangtze River Bridge in the haze, high-rise apartment blocks with few lights, a lone delivery rider on an electric scooter and a single worker in protective clothing far away, a temporary hospital of prefabricated blue-roofed units in the distance. Rendered as a quiet muted documentary watercolour, cool greys and pale blues, still atmosphere, no text.
beiting: 702 CE, Tingzhou (modern Jimsar) north of the Tianshan: a newly walled Tang frontier town of rammed-earth ramparts and gate towers stands on a green plain beneath the snowy Bogda peaks. Tang officials in round-collared robes and black futou caps receive Turkic chiefs in felt hats leading horses, while armoured garrison troops, camel caravans and herds of sheep cross the grassland. Wide steppe, clear morning light. Painted in the style of a Tang-dynasty Dunhuang cave mural, mineral blues and greens on an ochre ground, flaking pigment texture.
kaiyuan: 713 CE, Chang'an: a high view over the vast grid of the Tang capital, broad tree-lined Zhuque Avenue running to the palace city, walled wards, Buddhist pagodas such as the Big Wild Goose Pagoda, and the bustling East Market with camels, horse carts and merchants from the Silk Road. In a wine shop small scholars in futou caps raise cups and write verse on silk. Spring blossoms, warm afternoon. Painted as a Tang court painting in the blue-green manner of Li Sixun, mineral pigments on silk, fine gold outlines.
talas: 751 CE, the Talas River valley in Central Asia: on a wide grassy plain below rolling mountains, a Tang army in lamellar armour with red banners faces Abbasid horsemen under black banners, while Karluk Turkic cavalry on the flank turn away from the Tang lines. Dust clouds rise over the river, the armies seen from a distance as dense masses of spears. Late summer, harsh light. Painted in the style of a Dunhuang cave mural battle scene, mineral greens, ochre and faded red, flaking plaster texture.
an-lushan: Winter 755 CE, marching south from Fanyang across the North China Plain: an immense frontier army of Han, Sogdian, Khitan and Tongluo cavalry in lamellar armour rides in long columns under banners, war drums on carts, dust and smoke rising over frozen fields and distant walled towns. Bare trees, low grey sky, villagers watching from afar. Painted in Tang-dynasty mural style like the Li Xian tomb procession frescoes, earthy reds and greens on plaster, bold outlines.
mawei: 756 CE, Mawei post station west of Chang'an: the fleeing imperial procession has halted in a dusty courtyard of a modest relay station; weary guards in armour hold spears and refuse to move, court ladies huddle beside a covered carriage, the elderly emperor stands small and distant beneath the eaves, and a Buddhist shrine with a pear tree stands at the edge of the yard. Overcast summer day, loess hills behind. Painted as a Tang-style handscroll in the manner of Emperor Minghuang's Journey to Shu, blue-green mountains, mineral pigments on silk.
tibet-changan: 763 CE, Chang'an: Tibetan imperial cavalry in chainmail and lamellar armour with long cloaks and tall banners ride through a great gate of the Tang capital, while plumes of smoke rise from palace halls and empty walled wards behind; townspeople flee along wide avenues toward the southern hills. Autumn, hazy sky. Painted in the manner of a Dunhuang cave mural, muted mineral greens and earth reds, small figures, flaking surface.
two-tax: 780 CE, Chang'an: in the courtyard of a Tang government granary, clerks in green robes and black futou caps weigh strings of bronze coins and measure bolts of silk and sacks of grain brought by farmers and landowners, scales and ledgers on low tables, ox carts queuing at the gate, tiled granary roofs beyond. Harvest season, soft afternoon light. Painted in Tang court painting style reminiscent of Zhang Xuan, fine line and gentle mineral colours on silk.
dunhuang-tibet: 786 CE, Dunhuang (Shazhou): Tibetan army tents and horse lines encircle the weathered rammed-earth walls of the oasis city after a long siege, while the gates open and townspeople and Tang officials file out to surrender; poplar groves, irrigation channels, the golden Mingsha sand dunes and the cliff of the Mogao caves in the distance. Dry desert light. Painted as a Dunhuang cave mural, ochre ground, mineral blues and greens, flaking pigment texture.
huichang: 845 CE, Chang'an: outside a great Buddhist monastery with a wooden pagoda, officials in robes and caps supervise workers lowering bronze Buddha statues and bells onto carts to be melted for coin, while long lines of monks and nuns in grey robes walk out of the gate carrying small bundles. Autumn trees, quiet dusty street, tiled roofs. Painted in late Tang court painting style, ink and muted mineral colours on silk, many small figures.
zhang-yichao: 848 CE, Dunhuang: a grand procession of mounted soldiers with banners, drummers and musicians escorts a commander on a white horse across the desert toward the oasis city gates, while Tibetan garrison troops withdraw into the distance; poplars, sand dunes and the Mogao cliff on the horizon. Bright desert morning. Painted in the style of the Zhang Yichao procession mural in Mogao Cave 156, mineral greens, reds and ochre on plaster, rhythmic rows of horsemen.
diamond-sutra: 868 CE, a printing workshop near Dunhuang: an artisan carves a large pear-wood block while another inks it and lifts a sheet of paper printed with a frontispiece picture of the Buddha preaching to monks under a canopy; finished panels are glued into a long scroll, characters too small to be legible.
