Oil lamp light, brushes and ink pots. Painted in late Tang Dunhuang mural style, warm ochre and mineral blue, softly worn surface.
huang-chao: 875 CE, Caozhou in Shandong: on the flat drought-stricken plain, a crowd of ragged peasants with hoes, staves and banners gathers around salt smugglers' carts piled with sacks, a leader on horseback addressing them from a dike; cracked fields, withered trees and a distant walled county town under a dusty yellow sky. Painted in late Tang style ink and light colour on silk, loose expressive brushwork, many small figures.
guangzhou-sack: 879 CE, Guangzhou on the Pearl River: seen from across the water, columns of smoke rise over the walled southern port, while ocean-going ships with matting sails and Arab dhows crowd the harbour and some flee downriver; rebel soldiers swarm along the riverbank and city gates, warehouses and banyan trees beyond. Humid, hazy afternoon. Painted as a late Tang ink-and-colour handscroll on silk, mineral greens, figures small and distant.
huang-chao-changan: 880 CE, Chang'an in winter: a huge rebel army in mixed armour and plain clothes enters the main gate of the Tang capital under banners, as officials in court robes kneel along the avenue to greet it; in the far distance a small imperial party on horseback hurries through snowy hills toward the mountain roads to Sichuan. Grey sky, empty wards. Painted in late Tang court style, ink and mineral colours on silk, panoramic composition.
end-of-tang: 907 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): in a great hall of a palace, ranks of officials in purple and red robes and black caps stand in rows as Tang court officers present the imperial seals and regalia on lacquered trays to a powerful warlord seated small and distant on a dais; armed guards line the hall, red pillars, bronze incense burners. Dim formal light. Painted in Five Dynasties court figure-painting style, as in The Night Revels of Han Xizai, fine line and rich colour on silk.
abaoji: 916 CE, the Khitan heartland near Shangjing (Linhuang): on a broad grassland by a river, Khitan nobles with shaved crowns and side locks, wearing left-closing robes and boots, gather before a great felt tent with banners and tall drums for an enthronement ceremony; horsemen, ox carts with felt covers, herds of horses and a white horse and grey ox for sacrifice. Wide sky, late summer. Painted in the style of Hu Gui's Khitan horsemen paintings, ink and colour on silk, fine detailed figures.
later-tang: 923 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): Shatuo Turkic cavalry in lamellar armour with bows and lances ride in a long column through the gate of the walled city on the Bian canal, banners streaming, while townspeople watch from tiled houses and boats on the canal; the old palace roofs in the distance. Autumn, clear light. Painted in Five Dynasties style like Hu Gui's horsemen, fine ink line with light colour on silk, energetic horses.
shu-conquered: 925 CE, Sichuan: a Later Tang army in armour winds along cliffside plank roads through the dramatic Jianmen Pass, then descends toward the green Chengdu Plain where the walled city of Chengdu stands among rice paddies and rivers; officials come out of the gate with offerings to surrender. Misty mountains, early winter. Painted as a monumental Five Dynasties landscape in the manner of Jing Hao and Guan Tong, ink on silk with light colour, tiny figures.
balhae-falls: 926 CE, Sanggyeong (near Ning'an, Heilongjiang): Khitan cavalry with shaved crowns and side locks surround the stone-founded walls and palace halls of the Balhae capital in a forested river valley, smoke rising from the gates, while a long line of Balhae officials in robes comes out to submit. Snow on the hills, cold winter light, wide northern landscape. Painted in the style of Hu Gui's Khitan scenes, ink and light colour on silk.
later-shu: 934 CE, Chengdu: a calm, prosperous court scene in a palace garden on the Chengdu Plain, a new ruler seated small on a dais among officials in robes; around the palace walls lie rice fields, brocade workshops with silk drying on frames, river boats and green hills. Spring sunshine, peaceful mood. Painted in Five Dynasties court style of the Shu painters such as Huang Quan, fine line, bright colours on silk, flowering trees.
sixteen-prefectures: 936 CE, near Youzhou (modern Beijing): in a Khitan felt-tent camp below the mountain passes of the north, envoys in Chinese court robes bow and present bundled maps and registers on trays to Khitan nobles with shaved crowns and side locks, while Khitan horsemen stand in ranks and carts of tribute silk wait nearby. Rugged Yanshan ridges and walled towns in the distance, autumn. Painted in Five Dynasties ink and colour on silk in the manner of Hu Gui.
southern-tang: 937 CE, Jinling (Nanjing): a palace of the new Southern Tang beside the Qinhuai River, with the Purple Mountain behind and the broad Yangtze in the distance; courtiers in elegant robes gather in a hall with painted screens and musicians, while boats glide on the river below. Soft spring evening light. Painted in the refined style of Southern Tang court painting like The Night Revels of Han Xizai, fine line, rich mineral colours on silk.
bach-dang: 938 CE, the Bạch Đằng River estuary in northern Vietnam: at low tide, rows of iron-tipped wooden stakes emerge from the muddy river, and a fleet of Southern Han warships with matting sails is caught and tilted among them, while small Vietnamese boats close in from mangrove banks under limestone hills. Grey morning mist, distant. Painted in a traditional ink and light colour handscroll style on silk, loose wet brushwork, small boats and figures.
min-divided: 945 CE, Fuzhou in Min: the walled city between its three hills and the White Pagoda, the Min River and its boats below, with armies of Southern Tang soldiers in lamellar armour approaching from the western mountains and a Wuyue fleet arriving by sea; smoke rising over a city worn by civil war. Subtropical green hills, cloudy sky. Painted in Five Dynasties monumental landscape style, ink and light colour on silk, tiny figures.
liao-takes-kaifeng: Early 947 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): Khitan horsemen with shaved crowns and side locks, fur-lined robes and bows ride through the wide snowy streets of the walled capital toward the palace, while officials of the defeated Later Jin kneel along the road in robes; camel carts with felt covers follow. Cold winter light, bare willows along the canal. Painted in Hu Gui's Khitan style, ink and colour on silk, fine detailed horses.
later-han: 947 CE, Taiyuan (Jinyang): the walled city on the Fen River below the Lüliang mountains; inside the gate, Shatuo Turkic troops in lamellar armour and Chinese officials in robes stand in ranks as their governor is acclaimed before a hall, banners and drums raised. Spring, loess terraces and willows beyond the walls. Painted as a Northern-style Five Dynasties landscape in the manner of Guan Tong, ink and colour on silk, small figures.
later-zhou: 951 CE, Bianzhou (Kaifeng): a column of soldiers escorts a mounted general through the city gate, one soldier having draped a torn yellow banner over his shoulders like a robe, while officials in court dress await him at the palace gate; canal boats and tiled roofs line the Bian River. Winter morning, pale light. Painted in Five Dynasties court style, fine ink line with light colour on silk, many small figures.
chu-falls: 951 CE, Changsha on the Xiang River: Southern Tang war boats with sails and oars come up the river toward the walled city of Chu, while soldiers march along the bank below Yuelu Mountain; smoke rises from a palace district damaged by fighting between rival princes. Lush green hills, humid haze. Painted in the manner of Southern Tang river landscapes like Zhao Gan's Along the River, ink and light colour on silk.
gaoping: 954 CE, Gaoping in southern Shanxi: on a valley floor among loess hills, the Later Zhou army in lamellar armour charges under red banners, a young ruler on horseback leading the guard at the front; the opposing Northern Han infantry and Khitan cavalry with shaved crowns waver and break in the dust. Seen from a hillside at a distance, spring. Painted as a Northern Song style battle handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, many small horsemen.
huainan-campaign: 956 CE, Shouzhou (Shouxian) on the Huai River: the Later Zhou army besieges the strong walled city, siege towers and battering rams at the gates, war boats blocking the river, camps and banners covering the plain; defenders on the walls with bows. Rain clouds, flooded fields, spring. Painted as a Five Dynasties monumental landscape in the manner of Guan Tong, ink and colour on silk, small figures in a broad scene.
chenqiao: 960 CE, Chenqiao post station north of Kaifeng: at dawn in a camp of tents and horses, armoured soldiers crowd around their general in front of the station gate and drape a yellow robe over his shoulders, officers kneeling, banners raised, frosty fields and bare willows beyond. Figures small, seen from a distance. Painted in early Northern Song figure-painting style, ink and light colour on silk, fine line, crisp winter light.
gaoliang: 979 CE, by the Gaoliang River outside Youzhou (Beijing): a Song army retreats in disorder across marshy plains as Khitan Liao cavalry with shaved crowns and side locks sweep in from both flanks, dust and smoke rising; the walled city of Youzhou and the Western Hills in the distance. Late summer evening, dramatic sky. Painted as a Northern Song battle handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, figures tiny within the landscape.
chanyuan: 1005 CE, Chanzhou (Puyang) on the Yellow River: Song and Liao envoys in contrasting robes meet beneath a pavilion between two armies encamped on either side of the river, while carts loaded with bolts of silk and silver ingots wait nearby; the Song emperor stands small on the city wall under a yellow canopy. Winter, ice on the river, pale sun. Painted as a Northern Song handscroll, ink and light colour on silk.
xixia: 1038 CE, Xingqing (Yinchuan): beneath the rugged Helan Mountains, the walled Tangut capital with its palace and white brick pagodas; Tangut nobles with shaved crowns and fringe hairstyles, in narrow-sleeved robes, assemble in a palace courtyard for a coronation, horsemen and camels outside the walls, the Yellow River and irrigated fields nearby. Clear autumn light. Painted in the style of Western Xia murals at the Yulin caves, mineral greens and earth reds on plaster.
movable-type: 1041 CE, a printer's workshop in Hangzhou: a commoner in a plain robe sets small fired-clay type pieces into an iron frame on a heated iron plate coated with pine resin and wax, trays of type pieces sorted in wooden cases, a second plate being inked, paper sheets drying on a line; characters are too small to read. Lattice windows, soft daylight. Painted in Northern Song genre style like the Qingming scroll, ink and light colour on silk, fine detail.
zizhi-tongjian: 1084 CE, Luoyang: in the study pavilion of a quiet scholar's garden with bamboo and a pond, an elderly scholar-official in a plain robe and cap sits at a desk surrounded by tall stacks of manuscripts and scroll boxes, assistants sorting drafts; the pages are blank or illegible. Autumn evening, lamp light through lattice windows. Painted in Northern Song literati style, ink and light colour on silk, delicate line and soft washes.
jurchen-jin: 1115 CE, Huining near the Anchuhu River in Manchuria: Jurchen warriors with shaved crowns and long braids, in fur and leather, gather on horseback in a forest clearing before a chieftain's hall of logs, raising banners and bows to acclaim their leader; birch and pine forests, a river, snow on the ground. Cold clear morning. Painted in Jin-dynasty figure-painting style like Zhang Yu's Wenji Returning to Han, ink and colour on silk, detailed horses and costume.
jingkang: 1127 CE, Kaifeng in winter: seen from a distance, a long column of Jurchen Jin cavalry escorts carts loaded with treasure, books and ritual bronzes and a line of captive courtiers north out of the city gate across a snowy plain; smoke rises over the walls and palace roofs of the fallen capital. Grey sky, falling snow. Painted as a Song-dynasty handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, tiny figures in a vast bleak landscape.
linan: 1138 CE, Lin'an (Hangzhou): West Lake surrounded by misty hills, pagodas, temples and willows on the causeways; pleasure boats on the water, and the walled city with crowded streets, shops and the palace on Phoenix Hill stretching toward the Qiantang River. Morning mist, spring. Painted in Southern Song style after Li Song's West Lake handscrolls and Ma Yuan's one-corner compositions, ink and pale colour on silk.
yue-fei: Winter 1142 CE, Lin'an (Hangzhou): a quiet, snow-covered courtyard of a government prison at night, a single lantern glowing under the eaves; inside an empty cell, a general's armour, helmet and spear lie set aside on a wooden rack, while outside the city walls West Lake and bare hills lie under snow. Solemn and still, no figures close up. Painted in Southern Song style after Ma Yuan and Xia Gui, ink washes on silk, much empty space.
caishi: 1161 CE, the Yangtze at Caishi below the Ma'anshan cliffs: Song treadle-powered paddle-wheel warships with wooden superstructures ram and scatter small Jin boats crossing the wide river, gunpowder thunderclap bombs bursting in clouds of lime smoke; Jin cavalry and tents crowd the far northern bank. Late autumn, windy sky. Painted in Southern Song style after Xia Gui, ink and light colour on silk, distant boats and figures.
genghis: 1206 CE, the source of the Onon River in Mongolia: a great assembly of Mongol chiefs and warriors on horseback surrounds a large white felt ger and a white standard of nine yak-tail banners; a small figure in fur-trimmed robe stands at the centre as nobles kneel. Rolling green steppe, river, distant mountains, herds of horses. Clear summer day. Painted in Yuan-dynasty handscroll style like Liu Guandao's Kublai Khan Hunting, ink and colour on silk.
caizhou: 1234 CE, Caizhou (Runan): the walled city under siege in winter, Mongol cavalry camps and Song army tents with banners on opposite sides, siege engines at the gates and a breach in the walls; dark smoke rises from a palace hall inside the city. Snow on the plain, grey dawn light, seen from a distance. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll in ink and light colour on silk, small figures.
liangzhou-meeting: 1247 CE, Liangzhou (Wuwei) in the Hexi Corridor: an elderly Tibetan lama in red monastic robes and a pointed scholar's hat, with young novices, is received in a large Mongol tent palace by a Mongol prince and his court in fur-trimmed robes; Buddhist offerings and silk hangings, camels and horses outside, snowy Qilian Mountains beyond. Painted in Tibetan thangka style of the Sakya tradition, mineral pigments, gold highlights, flat figures, no inscriptions.
xuanzheng: 1264 CE, the Mongol court at Yanjing (later Dadu, Beijing): in a palace hall hung with Buddhist banners, a young Tibetan lama in red robes is honoured by Mongol officials in fur-trimmed robes and Chinese scribes, while Tibetan monks and envoys bearing scarves wait in rows; lamps, gilded Buddha images, guards at the door. Painted in a Yuan-dynasty court style blended with Tibetan thangka colouring, mineral pigments and gold on silk.
kublai: 1271 CE, Dadu (Beijing): construction of a vast new capital, labourers raising rammed-earth walls and gates on a planned grid, palace halls with glazed roofs rising beside the Taiye Lake and the island of Qionghua; Mongol officials on horseback and Chinese architects inspect the work, camel caravans and carts bring timber. Clear autumn sky, Western Hills behind. Painted in Yuan-dynasty ruled-line architectural painting style, ink and colour on silk.
xiangyang: 1273 CE, Xiangyang on the Han River: huge counterweight trebuchets built by Muslim engineers hurl stones at the walls and towers of the fortress city from across the river, while Mongol armies and boats surround it, and Fancheng on the opposite bank has already fallen; dust and smoke at the walls, seen from a distance. Winter, hazy light. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty handscroll, ink and light colour on silk, small figures.
marco-polo: 1275 CE, Shangdu (Xanadu) on the Inner Mongolian grassland: the summer capital's walls and palace with a great tent pavilion; a small group of European travellers in Venetian tunics and caps, dusty from the road, kneel among a crowd of Mongol nobles, Tibetan monks and Persian officials before the distant throne. Horses, white mares, green steppe and blue summer sky. Painted in Yuan-dynasty court painting style like Liu Guandao, ink and colour on silk.
yamen: 1279 CE, Yamen on the coast of Guangdong: seen from a high headland, a great fleet of Song ships lashed together in the bay is broken by Yuan warships; burning sails and smoke drift over grey waves, and sea cliffs rise on both sides of the inlet. Stormy dusk, dramatic clouds, figures tiny and distant. Painted as a Yuan-dynasty ink landscape handscroll, ink washes and light colour on silk, mournful atmosphere.
japan-invasion: 1281 CE, Hakata Bay in Kyushu: a violent typhoon strikes a vast Yuan fleet of Chinese and Korean junks with matting sails at anchor near the islands; masts snap, ships collide and founder in towering waves, while samurai behind a long stone defensive wall on the shore watch from afar. Dark storm sky, rain, night falling. Painted in the style of the Japanese thirteenth-century Mōko Shūrai Ekotoba handscroll, ink and colour on paper, no inscriptions.
red-turbans: 1351 CE, the Yellow River dikes near Yingzhou: thousands of conscripted labourers with baskets, shovels and carrying poles repair a vast earthen dike, while some throw down their tools and gather around leaders wearing red headcloths, red banners raised; Yuan overseers on horseback in the distance. Muddy river, grey spring sky, flat plain. Painted in late Yuan to early Ming woodblock-print illustration style, bold black lines with light colour washes.
